a high power rocket launched from a facility or place in Australia.

part.heading: Regulation of space activities and high power rockets

content.p: Repeal the section, substitute:
• The operation of a launch facility in Australia requires a launch facility licence.

• A launch of a space object from a launch facility in Australia, from an Australian aircraft that is in flight or from a foreign aircraft that is in the airspace over Australian territory requires an Australian launch permit or an authorisation certificate.
• A launch of a high power rocket from a facility or place in Australia requires an Australian high power rocket permit or an authorisation certificate.
• A launch of a space object from a facility or place outside Australia by an Australian national requires an overseas payload permit or an authorisation certificate.
• A return of a space object to a place or area in Australia requires an Australian launch permit, a return authorisation or an authorisation certificate.
• A return of a space object to a place or area outside Australia by an Australian national requires a return authorisation or an authorisation certificate.
• The Minister may take into account the security, defence or international relations of Australia in deciding whether to grant a licence, permit or authorisation under this Part.
• The Minister is to appoint a Launch Safety Officer for certain space activities.

Repeal the sections, substitute:

section.heading: Launch facility licence required to operate a launch facility in Australia

content.p: A person must not operate a launch facility in Australia, or do anything directly connected with operating a launch facility in Australia, unless:
the person holds a launch facility licence for the launch facility; or
the person is a related party, for any launches conducted from the facility, of a person who holds such a licence; or
the person is acting as an employee, contractor or agent of a person who holds such a licence; or
an authorisation certificate covering the operation of the facility, or the things connected with the operation, is held by any person.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Launch of space object from Australian launch facility, Australian aircraft or foreign aircraft in airspace over Australian territory

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person:
launches a space object from a launch facility in Australia; or
launches a space object from an Australian aircraft that is in flight; or
launches a space object from a foreign aircraft that is in the airspace over Australian territory; and
the launch is not authorised by an Australian launch permit held by any person; and
no authorisation certificate covering the launch is held by any person.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Launch of high power rocket from Australia

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person launches a high power rocket from a facility (whether fixed or mobile), or place, in Australia; and
the launch is not authorised by an Australian high power rocket permit held by any person; and
no authorisation certificate covering the launch is held by any person.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Launch of space object from outside Australia

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
a space object is launched from a facility (whether fixed or mobile), or place, outside Australia; and
the person is a responsible party for the launch; and
the launch is not authorised by an overseas payload permit held by any person; and
no authorisation certificate covering the launch is held by any person.
Note: In this context, the effect of the definition of responsible party in section 8 is that the person is a responsible party only if the person is also an Australian national.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Return of space object to Australia

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
the person returns a space object to a place or area in Australia; and
the return of the object to that place or area is not authorised by an Australian launch permit held by any person; and
the return of the object to that place or area is not authorised by a return authorisation held by any person; and
no authorisation certificate covering the return is held by any person.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Return of space object outside Australia

content.p: A person commits an offence if:
a space object is returned to a place or area outside Australia; and
the person is a responsible party for the return; and
the return of the object to that place or area is not authorised by a return authorisation held by any person; and
no authorisation certificate covering the return is held by any person.
Note: In this context, the effect of the definition of responsible party in section 8 is that the person is a responsible party only if the person is also an Australian national.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.
Omit “space licence or launch permit”, substitute “launch facility licence or Australian launch permit”.
Repeal the Divisions, substitute:
The Minister may grant to a person a launch facility licence covering a particular launch facility in Australia if:
the Minister is satisfied that the person is competent to operate the launch facility; and

the Minister is satisfied that all necessary environmental approvals under Australian law have been obtained, and that an adequate environmental plan has been made, for the construction and operation of the launch facility; and
the Minister is satisfied that the person has sufficient funding to construct and operate the launch facility; and

the Minister is satisfied that the probability of the construction and operation of the launch facility causing substantial harm to public health or public safety or causing substantial damage to property is as low as is reasonably practicable; and
the Minister does not consider that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the launch facility licence should not be granted; and
the criteria (if any) prescribed by the rules are satisfied in relation to the launch facility.
A launch facility licence:
must specify the day on which it comes into force; and
remains in force for the period specified in the licence, which must be no longer than 20 years; and
is granted subject to the conditions in section 20 and any other conditions specified in the licence.
The following are conditions of each launch facility licence granted to a person, except to the extent that the licence otherwise specifies:
the holder of the licence must give the Minister any information that the Minister asks for under section 60 about the licence;
any other condition prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Breaching a launch facility licence condition

content.p: The holder of a launch facility licence must not contravene a condition of the licence.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
The Minister may, by written notice, transfer a launch facility licence to another person if the Minister could grant the licence to the other person under section 18.
Note: See section 25 for the procedure for transferring a launch facility licence.
The transfer takes effect at the time specified in the notice.
The Minister must give a copy of the notice to:
the holder of the licence immediately before the transfer; and
the other person.
The licence continues to cover the same launch facility.
The licence is subject to the same conditions as those in force immediately before the transfer (unless the Minister varies the conditions).
The period for which the licence remains in force continues to run despite the transfer.

section.heading: Varying or revoking a launch facility licence

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke a launch facility licence held by a person.
Note: See section 25 for the procedure for varying or revoking a launch facility licence.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Applying for the grant, variation or transfer of a launch facility licence

content.p: An application for the grant, variation or transfer of a launch facility licence must be made in accordance with the rules.
Without limiting subsection (1), the rules may provide for the lodging of documents at times worked out in accordance with the rules.
If the Minister considers that there may be grounds to vary, revoke or transfer a launch facility licence (other than at the licensee’s request), the Minister must:
give the licensee written notice of the Minister’s opinion specifying the reasons for that opinion; and
invite the licensee to make a written submission to the Minister about the matter within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
In deciding whether to vary, revoke or transfer a launch facility licence, the Minister must consider the matters raised in any submission received within the period specified in the notice.
The Minister must not vary a launch facility licence in a way that changes the location of the licensed launch facility.
The rules may prescribe other ways in which the Minister must not vary a launch facility licence.
The Minister may, in writing, suspend a launch facility licence if:
the holder of the licence contravenes a condition of the licence; or
the Minister considers that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the licence should be suspended.
The Minister must give notice of the suspension to the holder of the licence. The notice must specify the day the suspension takes effect.
A launch facility licence has no effect while suspended, but the period for which it remains in force continues to run despite the suspension.
The Minister may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Minister must give notice of the revocation to the holder of the licence. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Minister may vary or revoke a launch facility licence even while it is suspended.

section.heading: Basis on which launch facility licence is granted

content.p: A launch facility licence is granted on the basis that:
the licence may be transferred under section 22; and
the licence may be revoked under section 23; and
the licence may be varied under section 23; and
the licence may be suspended under section 26; and
the licence may be transferred, revoked, varied or suspended by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the licence is transferred, revoked, varied or suspended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.
The Minister may grant to a person an Australian launch permit authorising:
the launch of one or more space objects; or

a particular series of launches of space objects that, in the Minister’s opinion, having regard to the nature of any payloads to be carried, may appropriately be authorised by a single Australian launch permit;
from a specified launch facility in Australia, a specified Australian aircraft that is in flight or a specified foreign aircraft that is in the airspace over Australian territory.
The Australian launch permit may also authorise one or more space objects to be returned, in connection with the launch or launches, to a specified place or area in Australia.

Note: A returning space object need not be the same as the space object launched. For example, a launch vehicle could carry a payload into an area beyond the distance of 100 km above mean sea level and return without it, or even collect a different payload from an area beyond the distance of 100 km above mean sea level and return that to Earth.
The Minister may grant the Australian launch permit to the person only if all of the following criteria are met:
the Minister is satisfied that the person who is to carry out the launch or launches, and any connected return, is competent to do so;
the Minister is satisfied that the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 will be satisfied for the launch or launches, and any connected return;

the Minister is satisfied that the probability of the launch or launches, or any connected return, causing substantial harm to public health or public safety or causing substantial damage to property is as low as is reasonably practicable;
the space object or objects concerned are not and do not contain a nuclear weapon or a weapon of mass destruction of any other kind;
the Minister does not consider that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should not be granted;
any other criteria prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.
If a foreign country is also a launching State for the space object or any of the space objects, the Minister may, in deciding whether to grant the Australian launch permit, have regard to:

whether there is an agreement between Australia and that foreign country under which that foreign country assumes any liability, and indemnifies Australia, for any damage that the space object or objects may cause; and
the terms of that agreement.
Subsections (3) and (4) do not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard.
An Australian launch permit authorising the launch of a space object or objects, and any connected return:
must specify the day on which the permit comes into force and the period for which it remains in force; and
is granted subject to the conditions in section 30 and any other conditions specified in the permit.

An Australian launch permit may specify that the period for which it remains in force ends on the occurrence of a particular event (rather than at a specified time). For this purpose, the rules may set out how to determine when events of a particular kind occur.
Example: An Australian launch permit might specify that it expires when the relevant launch has been (successfully or unsuccessfully) completed. The rules could set out how to determine when this is.

At any time when an Australian launch permit is in force, the Minister may, by written notice given to the holder of the permit, extend or further extend the period for which the permit remains in force.
The following are conditions of each Australian launch permit, except to the extent that the permit otherwise specifies:
the launch or launches, and any connected return, must not be conducted in a way that is likely to cause substantial harm to public health or public safety or to cause substantial damage to property;
the space object or objects must not be or contain a nuclear weapon or a weapon of mass destruction of any other kind;
the space object or objects must not contain a nuclear power source unless the Minister’s written approval has first been obtained;
the holder of the permit must satisfy the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 for each launch, and each return, conducted under the permit;
any other conditions prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Breaching an Australian launch permit condition

content.p: Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is the holder of an Australian launch permit; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission contravenes a condition of the permit; and
the condition is a condition to which the permit is subject under paragraph 30(a), (b), (c) or (d).
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 year or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.
Civil penalty
The holder of an Australian launch permit must not contravene a condition of the permit.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
The Minister may, by written notice, transfer an Australian launch permit to another person if the Minister could grant the permit to the other person under section 28.
Note: See section 35 for the procedure for transferring an Australian launch permit.
The transfer takes effect at the time specified in the notice.
The Minister must give a copy of the notice to:
the holder of the permit immediately before the transfer; and
the other person.
The permit continues to cover the same launch facility, Australian aircraft or foreign aircraft and the same space object or objects.
The permit is subject to the same conditions as those in force immediately before the transfer (unless the Minister varies the conditions).
The period for which the permit remains in force continues to run despite the transfer.

section.heading: Varying or revoking an Australian launch permit

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke an Australian launch permit held by a person.
Note: See section 35 for the procedure for varying or revoking an Australian launch permit.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Applying for the grant, variation or transfer of an Australian launch permit

content.p: An application for the grant, variation or transfer of an Australian launch permit must be made in accordance with the rules.
Debris mitigation strategy
Without limiting subsection (1), an application for the grant of an Australian launch permit must include a strategy for debris mitigation.
The strategy must address the matters prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this subsection.
Subsection (3) does not limit the matters that may be included in the strategy.
If the Minister considers that there may be grounds to vary, revoke or transfer an Australian launch permit (other than at the permit holder’s request), the Minister must:
give the holder of the permit written notice of the Minister’s opinion specifying the reasons for that opinion; and
invite the holder to make a written submission to the Minister about the matter within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
In deciding whether to vary, revoke or transfer the permit, the Minister must consider the matters raised in any submission received within the period specified in the notice.
If the permit relates to a launch facility in Australia, the Minister must not vary the permit in a way that changes the location of the launch facility.
The rules may prescribe other ways in which the Minister must not vary an Australian launch permit.
The Minister may, in writing, suspend an Australian launch permit if:
the holder of the permit contravenes a condition of the permit; or
the Minister considers that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should be suspended; or
an incident involving a space object covered by the permit occurs during the liability period for the launch or return of the object.
The Minister must give notice of the suspension to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the suspension takes effect.
An Australian launch permit has no effect while suspended, but the period for which it remains in force continues to run despite the suspension.
The Minister may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Minister must give notice of the revocation to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Minister may vary or revoke an Australian launch permit even while it is suspended.

section.heading: Basis on which Australian launch permit is granted

content.p: An Australian launch permit is granted on the basis that:
the permit may be transferred under section 32; and
the permit may be revoked under section 33; and
the permit may be varied under section 33; and
the permit may be suspended under section 36; and
the permit may be transferred, revoked, varied or suspended by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the permit is transferred, revoked, varied or suspended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.

section.heading: Granting an Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: The Minister may grant to a person an Australian high power rocket permit authorising the launch of a high power rocket from a specified facility (whether fixed or mobile), or specified place, in Australia.
The Minister may grant the Australian high power rocket permit to the person only if all of the following criteria are met:
the Minister is satisfied that the person who is to carry out the launch is competent to do so;
the Minister is satisfied that the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 will be satisfied for the launch;

the Minister is satisfied that the probability of the launch causing substantial harm to public health or public safety or causing substantial damage to property is as low as is reasonably practicable;
the Minister does not consider that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should not be granted;
any other criteria prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Terms of Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: An Australian high power rocket permit authorising the launch of a high power rocket:
must specify the day on which the permit comes into force and the period for which it remains in force; and
is granted subject to the conditions in section 40 and any other conditions specified in the permit.

An Australian high power rocket permit may specify that the period for which it remains in force ends on the occurrence of a particular event (rather than at a specified time). For this purpose, the rules may set out how to determine when events of a particular kind occur.

Example: An Australian high power rocket permit might specify that it expires when the relevant launch has been (successfully or unsuccessfully) completed. The rules could set out how to determine when this is.

At any time when an Australian high power rocket permit is in force, the Minister may, by written notice given to the holder of the permit, extend or further extend the period for which the permit remains in force.

section.heading: Standard Australian high power rocket permit conditions

content.p: The following are conditions of each Australian high power rocket permit, except to the extent that the permit otherwise specifies:
the launch must not be conducted in a way that is likely to cause substantial harm to public health or public safety or to cause substantial damage to property;
the holder of the permit must satisfy the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 for the launch conducted under the permit;
any other conditions prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.

section.heading: Breaching an Australian high power rocket permit condition

content.p: Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person is the holder of an Australian high power rocket permit; and
the person does an act or omits to do an act; and
the act or omission contravenes a condition of the permit; and
the condition is a condition to which the permit is subject under paragraph 40(a) or (b).
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 year or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.
Civil penalty
The holder of an Australian high power rocket permit must not contravene a condition of the permit.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Transfer of Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: The Minister may, by written notice, transfer an Australian high power rocket permit to another person if the Minister could grant the permit to the other person under section 38.
Note: See section 45 for the procedure for transferring an Australian high power rocket permit.
The transfer takes effect at the time specified in the notice.
The Minister must give a copy of the notice to:
the holder of the permit immediately before the transfer; and
the other person.
The permit continues to cover the same facility or place and the same high power rocket.
The permit is subject to the same conditions as those in force immediately before the transfer (unless the Minister varies the conditions).
The period for which the permit remains in force continues to run despite the transfer.

section.heading: Varying or revoking an Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke an Australian high power rocket permit held by a person.
Note: See section 45 for the procedure for varying or revoking an Australian high power rocket permit.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Applying for the grant, variation or transfer of an Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: An application for the grant, variation or transfer of an Australian high power rocket permit must be made in accordance with the rules.
If the Minister considers that there may be grounds to vary, revoke or transfer an Australian high power rocket permit (other than at the permit holder’s request), the Minister must:
give the holder of the permit written notice of the Minister’s opinion specifying the reasons for that opinion; and
invite the holder to make a written submission to the Minister about the matter within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
In deciding whether to vary, revoke or transfer the permit, the Minister must consider the matters raised in any submission received within the period specified in the notice.
The rules may prescribe the ways in which the Minister must not vary an Australian high power rocket permit.

section.heading: Suspending an Australian high power rocket permit

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, suspend an Australian high power rocket permit if:
the holder of the permit contravenes a condition of the permit; or
the Minister considers that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should be suspended; or
an incident involving the high power rocket covered by the permit occurs during the liability period for the launch of the rocket.
The Minister must give notice of the suspension to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the suspension takes effect.
An Australian high power rocket permit has no effect while suspended, but the period for which it remains in force continues to run despite the suspension.
The Minister may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Minister must give notice of the revocation to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Minister may vary or revoke an Australian high power rocket permit even while it is suspended.

section.heading: Basis on which Australian high power rocket permit is granted

content.p: An Australian high power rocket permit is granted on the basis that:
the permit may be transferred under section 42; and
the permit may be revoked under section 43; and
the permit may be varied under section 43; and
the permit may be suspended under section 46; and
the permit may be transferred, revoked, varied or suspended by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the permit is transferred, revoked, varied or suspended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.
The Minister may grant to a person an overseas payload permit authorising:
the launch of one or more space objects; or

a particular series of launches of space objects that, in the Minister’s opinion, having regard to the nature of any payloads to be carried, may appropriately be authorised by a single overseas payload permit;
from a specified facility (whether fixed or mobile), or specified place, outside Australia using a specified launch vehicle.
Note: Overseas payload permits are required only if an Australian national would be a responsible party for the launch—see section 14.
The Minister may grant the overseas payload permit to the person only if all of the following criteria are met:
either:
the Minister is satisfied that the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 will be satisfied for each launch to be conducted under the permit; or
the Minister notifies the person, in writing, that, having regard to the nature and purpose of the space object or space objects concerned, those requirements are not required to be satisfied;
the Minister is satisfied that the probability of the launch or launches causing substantial harm to public health or public safety or causing substantial damage to property is sufficiently low;
the Minister does not consider that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should not be granted;
any other criteria prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.
The Minister may, in deciding whether to grant the overseas payload permit, have regard to:

whether there is an agreement or arrangement between Australia and the other launching State, or any of the other launching States, under which that State or those States assume liability, and indemnify Australia, for any damage that the space object or objects may cause; and
the terms of that agreement or arrangement.
Subsections (2) and (3) do not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard.
An overseas payload permit authorising the launch of a space object or objects:
must specify the day on which it comes into force and the period for which it remains in force; and
is granted subject to any conditions specified in the permit.

An overseas payload permit may specify that the period for which it remains in force ends on the occurrence of a particular event (rather than at a specified time). For this purpose, the rules may set out how to determine when events of a particular kind occur.

Example: An overseas payload permit might specify that its period expires when the relevant launch has been (successfully or unsuccessfully) completed. The rules could set out how to determine when this is.

At any time when an overseas payload permit is in force, the Minister may, by written notice given to the holder of the permit, extend or further extend the period for which the permit remains in force.

section.heading: Breaching an overseas payload permit condition

content.p: The holder of an overseas payload permit must not contravene a condition of the permit.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
The Minister may, by written notice, transfer an overseas payload permit to another person if the Minister could grant the permit to the other person under section 46B.
Note: See section 46H for the procedure for transferring an overseas payload permit.
The transfer takes effect at the time specified in the notice.
The Minister must give a copy of the notice to:
the holder of the permit immediately before the transfer; and
the other person.
The permit continues to cover the same facility or place, the same launch vehicle and the same space object or objects.
The permit is subject to the same conditions as those in force immediately before the transfer (unless the Minister varies the conditions).
The period for which the permit remains in force continues to run despite the transfer.

section.heading: Varying or revoking an overseas payload permit

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke an overseas payload permit held by a person.
Note: See section 46H for the procedure for varying or revoking an overseas payload permit.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Applying for the grant, variation or transfer of an overseas payload permit

content.p: An application for the grant, variation or transfer of an overseas payload permit must be made in accordance with the rules.
Debris mitigation strategy
Without limiting subsection (1), an application for the grant of an overseas payload permit must include a strategy for debris mitigation.
The strategy must address the matters prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this subsection.
Subsection (3) does not limit the matters that may be included in the strategy.
If the Minister considers that there may be grounds to vary, revoke or transfer an overseas payload permit (other than at the permit holder’s request), the Minister must:
give the holder of the permit written notice of the Minister’s opinion specifying the reasons for that opinion; and
invite the holder to make a written submission to the Minister about the matter within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
In deciding whether to vary, revoke or transfer the permit, the Minister must consider the matters raised in any submission received within the period specified in the notice.
The rules may prescribe the ways in which the Minister must not vary an overseas payload permit.
The Minister may, in writing, suspend an overseas payload permit if:
the holder of the permit contravenes a condition of the permit; or
if subparagraph 46B(2)(a)(i) applied—the Minister is satisfied that the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 are not satisfied for a launch to be conducted under the permit; or
the Minister considers that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the permit should be suspended.
The Minister must give notice of the suspension to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the suspension takes effect.
An overseas payload permit has no effect while suspended, but the period for which it remains in force continues to run despite the suspension.
The Minister may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Minister must give notice of the revocation to the holder of the permit. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Minister may vary or revoke an overseas payload permit even while it is suspended.

section.heading: Basis on which overseas payload permit is granted

content.p: An overseas payload permit is granted on the basis that:
the permit may be transferred under section 46E; and
the permit may be revoked under section 46F; and
the permit may be varied under section 46F; and
the permit may be suspended under section 46J; and
the permit may be transferred, revoked, varied or suspended by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the permit is transferred, revoked, varied or suspended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.
The Minister may give a person a return authorisation that authorises:
the return of a space object to a specified place or area in Australia or outside Australia; or
a particular series of such returns that, in the Minister’s opinion, having regard to the nature of the space objects to be returned, may appropriately be authorised by a single return authorisation.
The return or returns may be authorised under this section only if all of the following criteria are met:
the Minister is satisfied that the person who is to carry out the return or returns is competent to do so;
the Minister is satisfied that the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 will be satisfied for the return or returns;

the Minister is satisfied that the probability of the return or returns causing substantial harm to public health or public safety or causing substantial damage to property is as low as is reasonably practicable;
the space object or objects concerned are not and do not contain a nuclear weapon or a weapon of mass destruction of any other kind;
the Minister does not consider that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the authorisation should not be given;
any other criteria prescribed by the rules for the purposes of this paragraph.
The Minister may, in deciding whether to give a return authorisation, have regard to:

whether there is an agreement or arrangement between Australia and any country that is a launching State for any space object concerned under which that country assumes any liability, and indemnifies Australia, for any damage that the space object may cause; and
the terms of that agreement or arrangement.
Subsections (2) and (3) do not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard.
A return authorisation is subject to any conditions specified in the authorisation.

section.heading: Offence and civil penalty relating to returns

content.p: Offence
A person commits an offence if:
the person returns a space object purportedly in accordance with a return authorisation; and
one or more of the following applies:
the return is conducted in a way that is likely to cause substantial harm to public health or public safety or to cause substantial damage to property;
the space object is or contains a nuclear weapon or a weapon of mass destruction of any other kind;
the space object contains a nuclear power source and the Minister’s written approval for this has not first been obtained;
the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 are not satisfied for the return.
Penalty:
for an individual—imprisonment for 10 years or 5,500 penalty units, or both; or
for a body corporate—100,000 penalty units.
Civil penalty
A person must not return a space object purportedly in accordance with a return authorisation, in circumstances where one or more of the following applies:
the return is conducted in a way that is likely to cause substantial harm to public health or public safety or to cause substantial damage to property;
the space object is or contains a nuclear weapon or a weapon of mass destruction of any other kind;
the space object contains a nuclear power source and the Minister’s written approval for this has not first been obtained;
the insurance/financial requirements in Division 7 are not satisfied for the return.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.
The holder of a return authorisation must not contravene a condition of the authorisation.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Varying or revoking a return authorisation

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke a return authorisation held by a person.
Note: See section 46R for the procedure for varying or revoking a return authorisation.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Applying for the giving or variation of a return authorisation

content.p: An application for the giving or variation of a return authorisation must be made in accordance with the rules.
If the Minister considers that there may be grounds to vary or revoke a return authorisation (other than at the authorisation holder’s request), the Minister must:
give the holder of the authorisation written notice of the Minister’s opinion specifying the reasons for that opinion; and
invite the holder to make a written submission to the Minister about the matter within a reasonable period specified in the notice.
In deciding whether to vary or revoke the authorisation, the Minister must consider the matters raised in any submission received within the period specified in the notice.
The Minister may, in writing, suspend a return authorisation if:
the holder of the authorisation contravenes a condition of the authorisation; or
the Minister considers that, for reasons relevant to the security, defence or international relations of Australia, the authorisation should be suspended; or
an incident involving a space object covered by the authorisation occurs during the liability period for the return of the object.
The Minister must give notice of the suspension to the holder of the authorisation. The notice must specify the day the suspension takes effect.
A return authorisation has no effect while suspended.
The Minister may, in writing, revoke a suspension under subsection (1).
The Minister must give notice of the revocation to the holder of the authorisation. The notice must specify the day the revocation takes effect.
The Minister may vary or revoke a return authorisation even while it is suspended.

section.heading: Basis on which return authorisation is given

content.p: A return authorisation is given on the basis that:
the authorisation may be revoked under section 46P; and
the authorisation may be varied under section 46P; and
the authorisation may be suspended under section 46S; and
the authorisation may be revoked, varied or suspended by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the authorisation is revoked, varied or suspended as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.
The Minister may issue to any person an authorisation certificate covering specified conduct that might otherwise be prohibited by section 11, 12, 13, 14, 15 or 15A.
Note: Under subsection 33(3A) of the Acts Interpretation Act 1901, conduct may be specified by reference to a particular class or classes of conduct.
The rules may set out matters to which the Minister must have regard in deciding whether to issue an authorisation certificate.

Example: The rules might set out criteria such as whether a launch would be in the national interest or would confer a significant national benefit, whether there is a risk that a launch might cause substantial harm to public health or public safety or damage to property or whether there is a risk that a launch might expose the Commonwealth to liability for damage caused.
Subsection (2) does not limit the matters to which the Minister may have regard.
Within 7 sitting days of issuing an authorisation certificate, the Minister must cause a copy of the certificate to be tabled in each House of the Parliament.
An authorisation certificate:
comes into force on a specified day or when a specified event happens; and
remains in force for a specified period (which may be a period that ends on the occurrence of a specified event).
For the purposes of subsection (1), the rules may set out how to determine when events of a particular kind occur.
At any time when an authorisation certificate is in force, the Minister may, by written notice, extend or further extend the period for which the certificate remains in force.
An authorisation certificate is issued subject to any conditions specified in the certificate.
The holder of an authorisation certificate must not contravene a condition of the certificate.
Civil penalty: 1,000 penalty units.

section.heading: Varying or revoking an authorisation certificate

content.p: The Minister may, in writing, vary or revoke an authorisation certificate held by a person.
The Minister must give notice of the variation or revocation to the person. The notice must specify the day the variation or revocation takes effect.

section.heading: Basis on which authorisation certificate is issued

content.p: An authorisation certificate is issued on the basis that:
the certificate may be revoked under section 46X; and
the certificate may be varied under section 46X; and
the certificate may be revoked or varied by or under later legislation; and
no compensation is payable if the certificate is revoked or varied as mentioned in any of the above paragraphs.

part.heading: Liability for damage by high power rockets

content.p: • The launch party for the launch of a high power rocket is liable to pay compensation for any damage the rocket causes to a third party on Earth or in the air.
This Part applies to damage a high power rocket causes if:
the object is launched from a facility (whether fixed or mobile), or place, in Australia; and
the damage is caused during the liability period for the launch.
This Part applies to damage mentioned in subsection (1):
whether the damage happens on Earth or in the air; and
whether the damage happens in Australia or outside it; and
whether or not the launch was authorised under this Act; and
whether or not the launch was covered by an authorisation certificate.

section.heading: Compensation for third party damage by high power rockets to be determined solely under this Part

content.p: Compensation for damage to which this Part applies caused to third parties is only payable in accordance with this Part.

Note: This section does not affect the rights of persons who are not third parties (for example, employees of a launch party) from seeking compensation outside of this Act for damage to which this Part applies.

section.heading: Damage on Earth or in the air

content.p: The launch party for the launch of a high power rocket is liable to pay compensation for any damage the rocket causes to a third party on Earth or in the air.
However, the launch party is not liable to the extent that the launch party establishes that the damage resulted from:
the negligence of the third party; or
any conduct (whether by act or omission) that the third party engaged in with intent to cause the damage.

section.heading: Limit on amount of permit holder’s liability

content.p: This section applies if:
the launch of a high power rocket that causes damage to which this Part applies was authorised by an Australian high power rocket permit; and

the damage did not result from a breach of any of the conditions of the permit, from any conduct (whether by act or omission) that the launch party or a related party engaged in with intent to cause the damage or from the negligence of the launch party or a related party.
The launch party is not liable to pay compensation for the damage to the extent that the amount of the compensation would exceed the insured amount for the Australian high power rocket permit.
If:

The Consolidated Revenue Fund is appropriated for the purposes of payments by the Commonwealth under subsection (3).

section.heading: Federal Court and Federal Circuit Court have jurisdiction

content.p: The Federal Court and the Federal Circuit Court have jurisdiction to hear and determine actions for compensation for damage to which this Part applies.
An action for compensation for damage to which this Part applies may only be brought:
within 1 year after the day on which the damage occurred; or
if, when the damage occurred, the person bringing the action did not know that it had occurred—within 1 year after the day on which the person:
became aware of the damage; or
would have become aware of the damage, if the person had exercised due diligence.
